rationale: E. rectale ferments glucose and lactate via mixed-acid pathway, producing acetate, butyrate, formate, and CO₂. Glucose is the preferred substrate; lactate is oxidized as a secondary energy source. Amino acids (cysteine, serine) provide nitrogen and supplementary carbon. Ammonium is the primary nitrogen source. At 0.30 /h growth, carbon balance is maintained: 79.2 mmol C in (glucose, lactate, amino acids) minus 34 mmol C out (fermentation products) minus 9.9 mmol C for biomass = sustainable. Nitrogen: 2.9 mmol in, 2.1 mmol for growth, with small surplus.
